content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm seeking assistance with [product_name] analog value retention after a power interruption or restart. The custom parameters work fine until a power outage, at which point they reset to 0 after rebooting. I’ve tried several suggested methods but none have worked so far. Thank you.
I've attached a solution. Please check the [product_name] program for Parameter-VM-Mapping.

Hello [user_name], thanks for sharing your solution. I included the top analog marker to properly display the "Rainbow" effect with my 0 to 5V DC input. However, I’m still having trouble. When I input 80 in the upper parameter, the lower immediately shows 20500, and if I enter 20 in the lower, the upper resets to 0. Clearly, I’m missing something. Best regards.

Here's the issue: you requested a solution, I provided a correct one, but then you made changes. Why did you introduce AM3? Why did you input incorrect values into the tag table of the [product_name]? This created overlap with variables VW3 and VW4.

Thank you for your quick response and solution. I modified the solution because it did not retain the values after I powered down the [product_name]. I downloaded the solution for both [product_name] modules. I’ve attached a video showing how it behaves. I'm unsure where I went wrong.

I’m not experiencing the same issue as you. I also created a screen recording, and in my case, after a power outage, the values transferred from the web server to the [product_name] remain unchanged. During the online test, you can see I turned off the voltage and received a message indicating "Transmission failed".
Thank you for your time and help, I truly appreciate it. I'll dedicate some time this weekend to investigate what I'm doing incorrectly. Kind regards.

I've handled many projects like this, including for other forum users, and used both [company_name] panels and web servers—all work without issues. Double-check your tag table, the value for VW3 should actually be VW2.

Thank you—your solution is much better than my previous one, which reset all analog values to zero after a power outage. Currently, my values revert to a set default found in my [product_name] when I download the program. I've reviewed my setup but haven't found how to get it to behave like your example. Video had to be split; see next message for part two. Kind regards.
Here is the second part of the video. Thank you.
Have you saved the program to an SD card on the [product_name]?

I'm experiencing the same situation as [user_name]. I record the program to both SD card and [product_name], but I need its last values set in the web interface to persist after turning off and on again.
Please upload your program as a ZIP file to the forum. Also, did you save it on the SD card?

Hello [user_name], just wanted to share some feedback. I noticed if I modify values on the web page and then, on the [product_name], stop the program, save to the card, and restart, the updated values are retained even after a power failure. We need the full original large program (about 90 blocks) saved on the card to protect it before selling. I still need to figure out how to do that. Best regards.

That’s why I asked if you’re using an SD card. When a program is on the SD card, it loads from the card each time the [product_name] restarts. This means any parameter changes get overwritten. It’s not necessary to store the program on the SD card since the [product_name] has non-volatile memory.

Thank you for your response. Yes, I stored the program on the SD card to prevent unauthorized copying by other dealers. I’m still working on a way to protect the program but maintain access to parameters through the web page.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is struggling with retaining analog parameter values in [product_name] following power loss or restarts. When parameters are set via the web interface, they reset to zero or a default state, instead of maintaining the last user-set value. Suggested solutions haven’t resolved the issue, pointing to either configuration errors or misunderstandings about value retention in the [company_name] product environment. Forum members are trying to verify correct behavior and help correct user-side mistakes.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects analog values entered through the web interface on [product_name] to persist after power failures or device resets, retaining the most recent settings rather than reverting to factory defaults.
